Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2632; without (legal) trial:--uncondemned.
BiblicalUsage: Twice, both times Paul's Roman citizenship saves him. At Philippi he refuses a quiet release: They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison — and the magistrates come trembling to apologize.
TheologicalSignificance: A legal word for uncondemned carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the two scenes, where Paul's citizenship stops the scourge and shames the magistrates.
RelatedEvents: Paul and Silas in the Philippian Prison; Paul Claims Roman Citizenship
